name: Cups are spiders
summary: A bare cup is a phase-free Z-spider with two outputs.
description:
The cup (and, upside down, the cap) is the same as a phase-free spider with two legs on the same side. Together with [spider fusion](../spider-fusion/) this means that only the connectivity of a ZX-diagram matters: wires can be bent around freely (*only connectivity matters*).

In PyZX and ZXLive inputs and outputs are determined by their position, so a bare cup cannot be drawn directly; this axiom is built into the way diagrams are represented there.
unchecked_reason: a bare cup (a wire whose two ends are both outputs) cannot be represented with ZXLive-style boundaries
